Subject: Nectar Health — Inference deployment pathways and SLOs

Thanks again for taking the time today — summarized notes and proposed next steps below. Short version: primary pain is unpredictable inference cost at scale + 99th percentile latency spikes during daytime traffic. Goals are predictable per-tenant latency (p99 < 250ms for short responses), sustained throughput for peak windows, and an ops story that keeps PHI on-prem for regulated workflows.

Key pain points we heard
- Inference cost variance across peaks makes budgeting impossible
- Some endpoints must never traverse public networks (PHI)
- Model response quality regression after quantization has blocked past efforts

Agreed goals
- P99 latency target: < 250ms for 64–128 token responses for the clinical assistant routes
- Baseline throughput: 3,000 simultaneous requests (peaks) across all services, with burst to 5k for short windows
- Data isolation: private VPC for PHI routes + hosted fallback for non-PHI requests

Proposed next steps
1) Technical topology options from Redwood (target: 2026-09-02) — owner: Aditya (I looped him in).
2) Mutual action plan (legal/procurement) — I'll share an MPA draft; procurement to comment by 2026-09-09.
3) Short bench: Redwood will run a 5k-req latency benchmark against a representative prompt set; results shared 2026-09-04.

Attachments: nectar_mpa_draft.pdf (MPA skeleton), latency_benchmark_5kreqs.csv (sample bench format)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the timelines.

Great points — short answers here and an ask for the benchmark prompt set: please provide a 20–30 prompt sample (anonymized) that represents your typical clinical Q&A and a couple of long-form discharge summaries. We will run the 5k bench only against anonymized data or synthetic prompts unless you explicitly permit PHI for an on-prem run.

High-level network / KMS note
- Private VPC option: customer-managed VPC peering + transit gateway, no public egress for PHI routes. KMS: we support customer KMS keys (AWS KMS + external HSM integrations) for model keys and audit logs.
- Hosted fallback: requests routed by policy; PHI-tagged routes are pinned to private deployment and never egress to hosted tiers. We can share the exact ACLs/nat policies in the MPA appendix.

Model notes
- Recommended family: LLaMA-2 / Falcon class models sized 13B–33B for clinical fidelity; Redwood supports 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants with evaluation pipelines to measure quality drift.
- If you require the smallest inference footprint, we recommend a 13B 4-bit quantized profile with per-prompt evaluation keys to guard quality.

Next steps recap
- Aditya to provide two deployment pathways with cost/latency tradeoffs (due 2026-09-02).
- Procurement to return MPA comments by 2026-09-09.
- Nectar to send anonymized 20–30 prompt sample once procurement signs off.

Thanks — I’ll collect the anonymized prompts and confirm the bench window.

—

Hi Marcus / Priya — following up with two concrete deployment pathways and the expected SLO numbers. Numbers below assume 64–128 token median responses and the prompt mix you described.

Option A — Private VPC (customer-managed) + Local Dedicated Pods
- Topology: Private VPC peering -> dedicated Redwood cluster in your VPC -> Autoscale pool of GPU pods (per-region). No public egress for PHI routes.
- HW profile: mix of NVIDIA A10G (cost-sensitive) and H100 (latency-critical) nodes.
- Per-pod performance (13B 4-bit, sequence <=512): ~120 qps sustained on A10G; ~380 qps on H100 with batched inference (batch size 8).
- Expected p50/p90/p99 latency (512 token budget): A10G: 45ms / 110ms / 230ms; H100: 15ms / 35ms / 95ms.
- Operational notes: KV cache enabled per-tenant yields ~2x throughput improvement for conversational workloads. Requires ~8GB persistent cache per active conversation set.
- Cost posture: predictable monthly reserved capacity; estimated commit to cover 80% peak = 6 A10G pods + 3 H100 pods (ballpark).

Option B — Hybrid: Hosted control plane + Redwood Dedicated region + Smart Routing
- Topology: Private VPC connects to a dedicated Redwood tenancy in customer region; non-PHI requests may route to hosted pool when capacity constraints occur.
- HW profile: Dedicated H100 pool for p99-sensitive routes; hosted fallback uses smaller 13B quantized variants to lower cost.
- Routing policy: latency-first for clinical assistant routes, cost-first for analytics batch jobs. Automatic fallback to quantized hosted variant with model-verification guardrails.
- Per-pod perf (hosted 13B quantized): ~240 qps with p99 ~320ms for 512 token; not acceptable for clinical P99 target — use only for non-PHI fallback.

Quality controls and evals
- We’ll run A/B evals on your anonymized prompts across the candidate quantized profiles and flag regression > 2% quality delta vs baseline.

Bench plan
- Redwood to run the 5k-req bench on anonymized prompts in a fenced environment (no PHI egress). If you want a PHI-on-prem bench, we’ll run the same on your VPC cluster (no data leaves your network). Results due 2026-09-04.

Deliverables and owners
- Topology + cost sketch (this email): Aditya — done.
- Bench results (anonymized): Aditya / Redwood infra — 2026-09-04.
- MPA comments: Nectar procurement — 2026-09-09.

Attachments: nectar_mpa_draft.pdf (MPA skeleton)

If you want, I can package a one-page comparison table for both options and a recommended starting commit size tomorrow.
